concepts.title: Rooted forests through ancestor relations
concepts.description:
A strict ancestor relation of a rooted forest is transitive and irreflexive,
and the ancestors of each vertex are linearly ordered. On a finite vertex
set, these conditions characterize the strict ancestor relations of rooted
forests.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Rooted forests through ancestor relations
type: definition
---
A strict ancestor relation of a rooted forest is transitive and irreflexive,
and the ancestors of each vertex are linearly ordered. On a finite vertex
set, these conditions characterize the strict ancestor relations of rooted
forests.
-/

namespace Lax183560.AncestorForest

/-- A strict ancestor relation of a rooted forest on `V`. -/
structure AncestorForest (V : Type) where
  ancestor : V → V → Prop
  transitive : IsTrans V ancestor
  irreflexive : Std.Irrefl ancestor
  ancestors_linearly_ordered : ∀ u v w : V,
    (ancestor u w ∧ ancestor v w) → (u = v ∨ ancestor u v ∨ ancestor v u)


end Lax183560.AncestorForest

concepts.title: Binary branch decompositions of finite sets
concepts.description:
A branch decomposition of a finite set is an unrooted tree of maximum degree
three whose leaves are in bijection with the set. Each edge determines a cut
by separating the leaves into two parts.

For symmetric cut functions, a decomposition can be represented by a binary
tree obtained by rooting it at an edge. Each subtree determines one side of
a cut. The root determines the cut with an empty opposite side, which has
value zero for the cut functions used here.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Rank
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Binary branch decompositions of finite sets
type: definition
---
A branch decomposition of a finite set is an unrooted tree of maximum degree
three whose leaves are in bijection with the set. Each edge determines a cut
by separating the leaves into two parts.

For symmetric cut functions, a decomposition can be represented by a binary
tree obtained by rooting it at an edge. Each subtree determines one side of
a cut. The root determines the cut with an empty opposite side, which has
value zero for the cut functions used here.
-/

namespace Lax183560.BranchDecompositions

inductive BinaryTree (α : Type) where
  | leaf : α → BinaryTree α
  | fork : BinaryTree α → BinaryTree α → BinaryTree α

/-- Leaves with multiplicity, in left-to-right order. -/
def BinaryTree.leaves {α : Type} : BinaryTree α → List α
  | .leaf a => [a]
  | .fork left right => left.leaves ++ right.leaves

/-- A valid branch tree contains each element of the ground set once. -/
def BinaryTree.Valid {α : Type} [DecidableEq α]
    (t : BinaryTree α) (ground : Finset α) : Prop :=
  t.leaves.Nodup ∧ t.leaves.toFinset = ground

/-- Maximum cut value among the cuts at the nodes of a branch tree. -/
def BinaryTree.cutWidth {α : Type} [DecidableEq α]
    (measure : Finset α → ℕ) : BinaryTree α → ℕ
  | .leaf a => measure {a}
  | .fork left right =>
      max (measure ((left.leaves ++ right.leaves).toFinset))
        (max (left.cutWidth measure) (right.cutWidth measure))

end Lax183560.BranchDecompositions

concepts.title: Branchwidth
concepts.description:
The branchwidth of a graph is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of
its edge set, of the maximum size of a middle set. The middle set of a cut
consists of the vertices incident with an edge on each side of the cut.
Graphs with at most one edge have branchwidth zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.BranchDecompositions

/-!
---
title: Branchwidth
type: definition
---
The branchwidth of a graph is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of
its edge set, of the maximum size of a middle set. The middle set of a cut
consists of the vertices incident with an edge on each side of the cut.
Graphs with at most one edge have branchwidth zero.
-/

namespace Lax183560.Branchwidth

open Lax183560.BranchDecompositions

/-- Number of vertices incident with an edge in `A` and an edge outside `A`. -/
noncomputable def middleSize {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (A : Finset (Sym2 V)) : ℕ :=
  {v : V | (∃ e : Sym2 V, e ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ e ∈ A ∧ v ∈ e) ∧
    (∃ e : Sym2 V, e ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ e ∉ A ∧ v ∈ e)}.ncard

/-- A branch decomposition with every middle set of size at most `k`. -/
noncomputable def HasBranchwidthAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact G.edgeSet = ∅ ∨
    ∃ t : BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Sym2 V),
      t.Valid G.edgeFinset ∧
      t.cutWidth (middleSize G) ≤ k

/-- The minimum middle-set width of an edge branch decomposition. -/
noncomputable def branchwidth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasBranchwidthAtMost G k}

end Lax183560.Branchwidth

concepts.title: Binary cut-rank
concepts.description:
For a vertex set $A$ in a graph, the cut-rank is the rank over the
two-element field of the adjacency matrix with rows indexed by $A$ and
columns indexed by the vertices outside $A$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Rank
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic

/-!
---
title: Binary cut-rank
type: definition
---
For a vertex set $A$ in a graph, the cut-rank is the rank over the
two-element field of the adjacency matrix with rows indexed by $A$ and
columns indexed by the vertices outside $A$.
-/

namespace Lax183560.CutRank

/-- Binary rank of the adjacency matrix across a cut. -/
noncomputable def cutRank {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (A : Finset V) : ℕ := by
  classical
  let M : Matrix {v : V // v ∈ A} {v : V // v ∉ A} (ZMod 2) :=
    fun u v => if G.Adj u v then 1 else 0
  exact M.rank


end Lax183560.CutRank

concepts.title: Modular decompositions
concepts.description:
A modular decomposition recursively partitions a graph into nonempty modules.
A module is a vertex set whose vertices have the same neighbors outside the
set. Between any two parts, either all possible edges are present or none
are; a quotient graph records which parts are adjacent. Each part is
decomposed recursively, with graphs on at most one vertex as the base case.

A decomposition has width at most $k$ if every substitution uses at most
$k$ parts, except for disjoint unions and complete joins, whose numbers of
parts are unrestricted. The quotient graphs need not be prime.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps

/-!
---
title: Modular decompositions
type: definition
---
A modular decomposition recursively partitions a graph into nonempty modules.
A module is a vertex set whose vertices have the same neighbors outside the
set. Between any two parts, either all possible edges are present or none
are; a quotient graph records which parts are adjacent. Each part is
decomposed recursively, with graphs on at most one vertex as the base case.

A decomposition has width at most $k$ if every substitution uses at most
$k$ parts, except for disjoint unions and complete joins, whose numbers of
parts are unrestricted. The quotient graphs need not be prime.
-/

namespace Lax183560.ModularDecomposition

/-- A recursive modular decomposition whose nontrivial substitutions use at
most `k` parts. -/
inductive ModularDecomposition :
    (V : Type) → SimpleGraph V → ℕ → Prop where
  | atom {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
      (h : Fintype.card V ≤ 1) : ModularDecomposition V G k
  | substitute {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) (k n : ℕ)
      (part : V → Fin n) (Q : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
      (nontrivial : 2 ≤ n)
      (surjective : Function.Surjective part)
      (cross : ∀ u v : V, part u ≠ part v →
        (G.Adj u v ↔ Q.Adj (part u) (part v)))
      (children : ∀ i : Fin n,
        ModularDecomposition {v : V // part v = i}
          (G.induce {v : V | part v = i}) k)
      (arity : Q = ⊥ ∨ Q = ⊤ ∨ n ≤ k) :
      ModularDecomposition V G k


end Lax183560.ModularDecomposition

concepts.title: Modular-width
concepts.description:
The modular-width of a graph is the minimum, over all modular decompositions,
of the maximum number of parts in a substitution other than a disjoint union
or a complete join. Disjoint unions and complete joins do not contribute to
the width. Under this convention, cographs have modular-width zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.ModularDecomposition
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Modular-width
type: definition
---
The modular-width of a graph is the minimum, over all modular decompositions,
of the maximum number of parts in a substitution other than a disjoint union
or a complete join. Disjoint unions and complete joins do not contribute to
the width. Under this convention, cographs have modular-width zero.
-/

namespace Lax183560.ModularWidth

open Lax183560.ModularDecomposition

/-- Existence of a modular decomposition with substitution arity bounded by k. -/
def HasModularWidthAtMost (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ModularDecomposition V G k

/-- The least maximum arity of a non-union, non-join substitution. -/
noncomputable def modularWidth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasModularWidthAtMost V G k}

end Lax183560.ModularWidth

concepts.title: Path decompositions
concepts.description:
A path decomposition of a graph is a finite sequence of vertex bags such
that every vertex belongs to a bag, both endpoints of every edge belong to
a common bag, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form an interval.
The sequence may be empty when the graph has no vertices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Path decompositions
type: definition
---
A path decomposition of a graph is a finite sequence of vertex bags such
that every vertex belongs to a bag, both endpoints of every edge belong to
a common bag, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form an interval.
The sequence may be empty when the graph has no vertices.
-/

namespace Lax183560.PathDecomposition

/-- A path decomposition indexed by a finite linear order. -/
structure PathDecomposition {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  length : ℕ
  bag : Fin length → Finset V
  vertex_mem_bag : ∀ v : V, ∃ i, v ∈ bag i
  edge_mem_bag : ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ i, u ∈ bag i ∧ v ∈ bag i
  bag_indices_interval : ∀ v : V, ∀ i j l : Fin length,
    (i ≤ j ∧ j ≤ l ∧ v ∈ bag i ∧ v ∈ bag l) → v ∈ bag j


end Lax183560.PathDecomposition

concepts.title: Pathwidth
concepts.description:
The pathwidth of a graph is the minimum width of a path decomposition.
The width of a path decomposition is the maximum bag size minus one.
The empty graph has pathwidth zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.PathDecomposition
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Pathwidth
type: definition
---
The pathwidth of a graph is the minimum width of a path decomposition.
The width of a path decomposition is the maximum bag size minus one.
The empty graph has pathwidth zero.
-/

namespace Lax183560.Pathwidth

open Lax183560.PathDecomposition

/-- Existence of a path decomposition with bags of size at most `k + 1`. -/
def HasPathwidthAtMost {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ D : PathDecomposition G, ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ k + 1

/-- The minimum path-decomposition width. -/
noncomputable def pathwidth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasPathwidthAtMost G k}

end Lax183560.Pathwidth

concepts.title: Rank-width
concepts.description:
The rank-width of a graph is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of
its vertex set, of the maximum cut-rank. The cut-rank of a cut is the rank
over the two-element field of the adjacency matrix between its two sides.
The empty graph has rank-width zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.BranchDecompositions
import Lax183560.CutRank

/-!
---
title: Rank-width
type: definition
---
The rank-width of a graph is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of
its vertex set, of the maximum cut-rank. The cut-rank of a cut is the rank
over the two-element field of the adjacency matrix between its two sides.
The empty graph has rank-width zero.
-/

namespace Lax183560.Rankwidth

open Lax183560.BranchDecompositions Lax183560.CutRank

/-- Existence of a vertex branch decomposition of cut-rank at most `k`. -/
def HasRankwidthAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsEmpty V ∨
    ∃ t : BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree V,
      t.Valid Finset.univ ∧
      t.cutWidth (cutRank G) ≤ k

/-- The minimum maximum binary cut-rank. -/
noncomputable def rankwidth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasRankwidthAtMost G k}

end Lax183560.Rankwidth

concepts.title: Treedepth
concepts.description:
The treedepth of a graph is the minimum height of a rooted forest on its
vertex set whose closure contains the graph. The closure joins every vertex
to each of its ancestors, and height counts the vertices on a longest
root-to-leaf path. The empty graph has treedepth zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.AncestorForest
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Treedepth
type: definition
---
The treedepth of a graph is the minimum height of a rooted forest on its
vertex set whose closure contains the graph. The closure joins every vertex
to each of its ancestors, and height counts the vertices on a longest
root-to-leaf path. The empty graph has treedepth zero.
-/

namespace Lax183560.TreeDepth

open Lax183560.AncestorForest

/-- `G` lies in the closure of a forest of vertex height at most `k`. -/
def HasTreedepthAtMost {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : AncestorForest V,
    (∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, G.Adj u v → (F.ancestor u v ∨ F.ancestor v u)) ∧
    ∃ rank : V → Fin k,
      ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, F.ancestor u v → rank u < rank v

/-- The minimum height of a rooted forest whose closure contains `G`. -/
noncomputable def treedepth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasTreedepthAtMost G k}

end Lax183560.TreeDepth
